question: Does the dual-crossing entropy (polytrope) closure reach convergence parity, judged on the solver rather than on dex?
verdict_basis: Pre-registered rule: pass requires >=52/60 first-trial convergence. 44 of 60 stars ran before the job was stopped; 16 converged. The maximum still reachable is 16+16=32/60, below 52, so the decision is arithmetically settled and the remaining 16 stars cannot change it. Stopping here is an early stop on a determined outcome, not an early stop on an unfavourable trend.

failure_is_regime_localised.note: The closure passes only where it does not fire. Above 8000 K there is little convection in the modelled range, so the closure degenerates to the parity profile and every star converges. Wherever convection actually engages it destroys the start. Note 5500-7000 K fails 13/13 -- a regime the original v1/v2 work never examined, having been scoped to 7000-8000 K.

offline_context.note: 24x worse offline; the funnel was run anyway because the whole premise of the retest is that offline dex does not predict convergence.

why_the_family_is_capped.conclusion: Integrating any gradient in a predicted ln P coordinate is capped near 0.232 even with a perfect gradient, because the quadrature weights are differences of a predicted quantity. Parity, which never integrates, is at 0.068. The route is structurally disadvantaged independently of the closure physics.
